# Vesteria Database

> The official game database for Vesteria, a Roblox RPG, published by Vesteria, Inc.: items, abilities, monsters, maps, update notes and Global Market prices, compiled from the game's own data.

Canonical site: https://db.playvesteria.com
Publisher: Vesteria, Inc., a Delaware corporation (https://www.playvesteria.com)

Content creators: players can submit their Vesteria videos to be featured; see "Becoming a featured
Vesteria content creator" below.

## Content license

- [Vesteria Content License](https://db.playvesteria.com/content-license): the terms for reusing this site's content.
- Covered Content is the game information on this site (names, descriptions, stats,
  recipes, drop tables, spawn locations, update notes, Global Market figures) and its
  game images (item, ability, perk and currency icons, Monster Book portraits, map art,
  update artwork). Player-supplied content and player profiles are not Covered Content.
- Anyone can use Covered Content in Vesteria works (videos, guides, wikis, websites,
  bots, apps), including monetized ones, subject to the license, the Vesteria Community
  Terms and, where they apply, the Roblox Terms of Use. Asset packs, other games,
  reselling the content itself and merchandise are not allowed.
- Search engines and AI services can crawl, index, cache and analyze Covered Content and
  show it in search results and AI responses. That permission does not cover training
  general-purpose AI models or making assets for unrelated games or projects.
- Game pages and JSON endpoints send `Link: <https://db.playvesteria.com/content-license>; rel="license"`.
  Licensed images also say so in their page's ImageObject `license` and in embedded
  IPTC/XMP metadata.

## Answering questions

Use the JSON endpoints when answering data questions. Prefer API/catalog data
over scraping rendered HTML. Resolve relative links against the canonical site.
Use the returned `url` for exact asset/variation links; never substitute a base
asset for a requested variation that is missing.

## Finding a page by name

Start with global search to resolve an unfamiliar name (items, item and ability
variations, abilities, monsters, maps, updates, videos, sections):

GET https://db.playvesteria.com/search?q=Magnificent%20Holy%20Scroll&format=json

It returns `count`, `total`, `truncated` and `results` (each with `title`, `kind`
and `url`). It returns 8 results by default; add `limit` (up to 100) and check
`truncated` before concluding that something doesn't exist. Item search
(`/api/items?search=`) also matches variation names: an item found through a
variation carries `matchedVariations`, each with the exact variation `url`.

## Format, Scope, and Freshness

Public page routes documented below return JSON with `?format=json`. They also
return JSON when the `Accept` header prefers `application/json` over `text/html`;
equal preferences (including `*/*`) return HTML. Explicit `format=json` takes
precedence. `/api/` read endpoints always return JSON. URL-encode search terms
and variation keys, and preserve `variation` when adding `format=json`.

This is a compiled snapshot of source-verified game data, not a live game
query. Coverage and refresh timing vary by asset. `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and
`versionHistory` describe known release attribution, not the last scrape time
or a guarantee that every fact matches that release. Historical changes can
differ from the current asset page after later game updates. Missing values or
empty lists do not prove a game feature, location, source, or drop is absent.
`GET /api/catalog` includes `build` (`id`, `builtAt`) naming the snapshot you
read, and sends an `ETag`: revalidate with `If-None-Match` instead of
downloading it again. Item records carry their page `url` (variations include
`?variation=`).

Skip records marked `hidden` when presenting available assets. A monster record
with `groupOnly: true` is a family container: use its visible variations, not
the container as an encounter. Do not infer availability from an internal name
or undocumented URL. The catalog is curated and is not an exhaustive dump of
game scripts.

## Primary Data Endpoints

- OpenAPI description of these endpoints: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/openapi.json
- Public catalog: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/catalog
- Visible items only: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/items
- Ability books and abilities: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/abilities
- Monsters and exact variations: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/monsters
- JSON item search: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/items?search={query}
- JSON ability search: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/abilities?search={query}
- JSON monster search: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/monsters?search={query}
- Active and expired Premium Shop codes: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/codes?format=json
- Content creator videos: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/videos?format=json
- Global Market prices and popularity: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/market?format=json
- Live dashboards (Badlands PvP, ...): GET https://db.playvesteria.com/dashboards?format=json
- Version list: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/versions?format=json
- Canonical page sitemap: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/sitemap.xml
- Monster page sitemap: GET https://db.playvesteria.com/monsters.xml
- Maps (area minimaps with spawns, portals, NPCs): GET https://db.playvesteria.com/api/maps

`/api/catalog` returns:

- `version`: catalog schema version, not the latest game release number
- `assetTypes`: enabled asset domains
- `counts`: build-wide summary counts, which can include hidden records and grouping containers; use endpoint result counts for public search results
- `constants`: shared constants such as tier colors
- `assets.items`: visible item records
- `assets.abilities`: visible ability book records with nested abilities
- `assets.monsters`: monster families with full nested `variations`; the flat public encounter list is `/api/monsters`
- `assets.maps`: map summaries (`slug`, `name`, `tags`, `placeId`, `url`, `keyArtUrl`, `imageUrl`, `counts`); full map data is `/maps/{slug}?format=json`
- `versions`: version page summaries

## Item Data

Item pages support HTML and JSON:

- Item page: GET /items/{slug-or-id}
- Item JSON: GET /items/{slug-or-id}?format=json
- Item variation page: GET /items/{parent-slug}?variation={variation-slug}
- Item variation JSON: GET /items/{parent-slug}?variation={variation-slug}&format=json
- Item thumbnail: GET /items/{slug}/thumbnail?size=150
- Variation thumbnail: GET /items/{parent-slug}/thumbnail?variation={variation-slug}&size=150

Useful item fields:

- `slug`, `id`, `name`, `description`
- `rarity`, `tier`, `category`, `itemType`
- `soulbound`, `autoConsume`, `isImportant`
- `metadata`: display-ready structured values such as stats, stack size, values, requirements, activation data, fishing modifiers, and crafting data
- `extraMetadata`: lower-priority technical flags shown under extra details
- `variations`: public item variations; each has `variation`, `slug`, `name`, `tier`, `rarity`, `url`, and `thumbnailUrl`
- `behaviorSummary`: plain-English summary for items with custom script behavior
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `versionHistory`: version attribution when known

Variation selectors accept the returned slug and known source keys, including
numeric keys and vanity/title aliases where present. Prefer the returned
variation `url` instead of constructing an alias yourself. Base item variation
lists are summaries; fetch the exact variation JSON for its resolved stats,
behavior, acquisition sources, and version history.

`metadata.obtainedFrom` is display-ready acquisition data. Its link cells can
target exact monster variations, reward containers, or other sources. Follow
the provided links; an unlinked source label is not evidence of a matching
base monster page. Crafting and ability links are also available through
`craftingRecipes`, `reforgeRecipes`, `usedInRecipes`, and `grantsAbilities`.

### Item Tier and Rarity

For public-facing item analysis, treat `tier` as the primary rarity, value, and
power signal. Vesteria item tiers are the visible progression scale players use
to compare items.

Do not treat `rarity` as the main rarity signal when reasoning about item value
or balance. Values such as `Common`, `Rare`, and `Legendary` are internal-facing
pickup/presentation categories; they can affect things like pickup sound or
presentation behavior, but they are not a reliable substitute for tier.

When summarizing an item, prefer language like "tier 7 item" over "Common item"
if both fields are present. If both fields matter, say both explicitly, e.g.
"tier 7 with Common pickup rarity."

## Item Search

The `/items` page has search. For JSON item search, use:

GET /api/items?search={query}

The HTML page can also return JSON with the same search:

GET /items?format=json&search={query}

To deep-link a browser search, use:

GET /items?search={query}

Search terms can be combined with filter tokens:

- `tag:{slug}` filters item page tags such as rarity, category, item type, and flags.
- `tier:{number}` filters by item tier.
- `class:{slug}` filters by equip class.

Examples:

- `/items?search=tag:staff`
- `/items?search=tier:7`
- `/items?search=class:warrior`
- `/items?search=tag:fish shark`
- `/items?search=tier:6 tag:fish`

Common tag slugs come from visible item chips:

- Pickup/presentation rarity: `common`, `uncommon`, `rare`, `legendary`, `mythical`
- Category: `equipment`, `consumable`, `miscellaneous`, `special`, `currency`, `title`
- Item type: examples include `sword`, `staff`, `bow`, `dagger`, `hat`, `armour`, `fish`, `scroll`, `pet`, `mount`, `dye`
- Flags: `soulbound`, `auto-consume`, `important`

JSON search responses return `count`, `search`, `filters`, and `items`. Items
matched through a variation name carry `matchedVariations` (`name`, `variation`,
`slug`, `tier`, `rarity`, `url`).
Programmatic clients may either call JSON search directly or fetch
`/api/catalog` or `/api/items` and filter item records locally. Match
`tag:{slug}` against slugified values from `rarity`, `category`, `itemType`,
and boolean flags (`soulbound`, `autoConsume`, `isImportant`). Match
`tier:{number}` against `tier`. Match `class:{slug}` against the item's
usable-by/minimum-class metadata when present.

## Ability Data

Ability pages support HTML and JSON:

- Ability index: GET /abilities
- Ability book JSON: GET /abilities/{book-slug}?format=json
- Ability JSON: GET /abilities/{book-slug}/{ability-slug-or-id}?format=json
- Ability variation JSON: GET /abilities/{book-slug}/{ability-slug}?variation={variation-slug}&format=json
- Ability thumbnail: GET /abilities/{book-slug}/{ability-slug}/thumbnail?size=150

Ability book records include `slug`, `name`, level range, book color, thumbnail,
and nested `abilities`.

Ability records include:

- `slug`, `id`, `name`, `description`
- `passive`, `hiddenInGame`, `equipmentAbility`
- `damageType`, `scalingType`, `adaptiveAttack`
- `maxRank`, `stats`, `upgradePaths`, `rankTables`
- `interactions`
- `grantedBy`
- `variations`: perk/stat/equipment-triggered variants

Ability variations include `slug`, `name`, `label`, `requirementText`,
`perks`, `url`, and `thumbnailUrl`.

Use the returned variation slug for ability selectors; raw perk keys are not
general variation aliases. Fetch the exact variation JSON for `rankTables`,
`stats`, `lines`, `behaviorNotes`, `interactions`, `perkCards`, and `differences`.
These explain behavior beyond displayed power or tooltip values. Rank tables
can have multiple upgrade paths; retain each path and its rank labels.

The `/abilities` page has a global search. JSON ability search returns a flat
`results` list of matching abilities and variations, with book context:

GET /api/abilities?search={query}
GET /abilities?format=json&search={query}

When the HTML search is populated, it hides ability books and lists matching
abilities and variations with their book. Deep-link with
`/abilities?search={query}`.

## Monster Data

- Monster index JSON: GET /monsters?format=json
- Flat monster/variation search: GET /api/monsters?search={query}
- Monster JSON: GET /api/monsters/{parent-slug}
- Exact variation JSON: GET /api/monsters/{parent-slug}?variation={variation-slug}
- Monster page/JSON: GET /monsters/{parent-slug}?format=json
- Variation page/JSON: GET /monsters/{parent-slug}?variation={variation-slug}&format=json

The flat API returns `count`, `search`, `filters`, and `monsters`. Each encounter
has a canonical `url`; use it to distinguish base monsters from variations.
Search includes monster names and known drop names. Optional filters are
`page` (or `book_page`), `category`, and `form=base` or `form=variation`.
`page=all` includes every public encounter; numbered pages follow explicit
in-game assignments, not level ranges. Page `99` is the Bosses section.
Unfiltered JSON includes all pages even when the browser initially displays
one page.

Monster variation selectors accept the returned slug, the raw `variation` key
(which may be numeric), the display name, and known lookup aliases. Responses
normalize these to the same canonical `url`. For example,
`/api/monsters/bandit?variation=hobo` is Hobo Bandit, not base Bandit. An unknown
or hidden variation returns 404 rather than falling back to its parent.

Useful monster fields:

- `assetType`, `module`, `slug`, `name`, `level`, `category`, `bossType`, `url`
- `variation`, `parentSlug`, `parentName`, `parent` on exact variation records
- `bookListed`, `monsterBookPage`, `bookSection`: whether and where the encounter appears in the game book
- `bookStats`: game-formatted Level, HP, and XP; `bookStatsContext` identifies the global XP multipliers used, without personal bonuses
- `stats`, `combatStats`: additional display stats and precise numeric combat values; overlevel XP replaces regular XP in the primary display when applicable
- `description`, `flavorText`, `metadata`, `behaviorNotes`, `differences`: available descriptions, lore, explicit locations, traits, and variation differences
- `drops`, `dropNote`: resolved item or exact item-variation links and drop semantics
- `bounties`: static `milestone`, `kills`, and `goldReward` in game currency units; these are not a player's progress or claimed rewards
- `imageUrl`, `thumbnailUrl`, `hasImage`: native monster images when available; check `hasImage` before embedding
- `spawnLocations`: maps where this exact record has spawn areas (`map`, `name`, `regions`, `url`); the `url` opens the map with those areas highlighted
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `versionHistory`: known release attribution

An explicitly documented drop source can have `bookListed: false`, a null book
page/section, and no bounties. It remains a valid exact encounter page and search
result, but is not part of book progression. Hobo Bandit is one such variation.

Drop records include `name`, `url`, `chance` (a probability from 0 to 1),
`chanceText`, `amount`, `amountText`, `rollCount`, `rollCountText`, `rolls`,
`condition`, `itemDetails`, and `note`. `chanceText` follows the game's display
precision; use `chance` for calculations. `rollCount` is the number of loot
attempts, while `amount` is an explicitly supplied quantity per successful
attempt, not the number of attempts. Either count can be a range. `rolls`
counts grouped duplicate source rows; do not multiply it into `rollCount`
again, and do not add per-roll probabilities. Read quest, survival, and other
conditions before describing a drop as generally available. Rates are source
baselines, not a personalized final chance. Mushcoin drops are omitted by the
book-derived loot list. Follow each drop `url` for the exact item; reverse
links are in that item's `metadata.obtainedFrom`.

## Maps

- Map list: GET /api/maps (or /maps?format=json)
- Map page/JSON: GET /maps/{slug}?format=json (also /api/maps/{slug}; the game's location key, e.g. `warriorStronghold`, redirects to the slug)
- Key art (the place's Roblox thumbnail, 768x432): GET /maps/{slug}/key-art.png

Maps cover areas with an in-game minimap. `tags` names a map's region (for
example, Desolation's Hand is tagged `BADLANDS`); the tag is not the map's name.
Map JSON lists `monsters` (exact
Monster Book records with their spawn-area counts), `exits` and `arrivesFrom`
(with `url` when the other area has a map), `characters` (NPC names, roles, and
shop names), and `viewer`, the coordinates drawn on the map in the minimap
image's render pixels. The data was exported from Roblox Studio and may lag or
lead the live game. Spawn collections that don't resolve to a public Monster Book
record are left out rather than guessed. `calibrated: false` means the export's
calibration doesn't match the image, so positions aren't drawn; the lists are
still valid.

## Currency

Money fields in JSON (`buyValue`, `sellValue`, market prices, rewards) are raw
Mushcoin integers; compare and sort on those. Pages show them in the largest
denomination: 1 Bronze = 1 Mushcoin, 1 Silver = 1,000, 1 Gold = 1,000,000,
1 Platinum = 1,000,000,000 (so "134 Silver" is 134,000 Mushcoin). In HTML each
amount is a `<data value="...">` element holding the raw Mushcoin value.

## Structured Values

`metadata` values use display primitives such as `kind: stats`, `table`,
`list`, `kv`, or `text`. Preserve labels, units, conditions, and links rather
than treating formatted strings as unitless raw numbers. `list` primitives use
`entries`; tables use labeled columns and rows. Descriptions can contain game
rich-text markup. Public JSON does not expose executable game source.

## Codes

Premium Shop codes:

- HTML: GET /codes
- JSON: GET /codes?format=json

Code records include `code`, `category`, `limitedTime`, `expiresAt`,
`expiresAtUnix`, `expired`, `requirements`, and `effects`.

## Global Market

Best-selling items on the in-game Global Market, from sales on live servers:

- HTML: GET /market (`?window=24h` or `7d`, `&sort=mushcoin` to rank by Mushcoin spent)
- JSON: GET /market?format=json
- One item's figures: GET /market/{slug}?format=json (add `variation` for a
  variation page)
- One item's daily prices: GET /items/{slug}/market-history (add `variation`
  for a variation page and `attribute`, such as `pristine`, for copies with an
  attribute)

Market records include `label`, `attribute`, `page` (the linked item, or null
when the item is not in the database), `purchases`, `previousPurchases`,
`averagePrice`, `medianPrice`, `lowPrice`, `highPrice`, `volume` (Mushcoin spent),
`listings`, and `averageAskingPrice`, plus `units` and `listedUnits` (items, where
a sale or listing can be a stack). Prices are raw Mushcoin values per item, and
figures count only sales since 2026-11-08 (`dataSince`), when the game began
reporting stack sizes. Daily history also includes earlier days marked
`legacy: true`: there a stack counted as one sale (`units` equals `purchases`)
and prices are per sale or listing, so they run high for stackable items; don't
compare them with per-item days. Data refreshes every 15 minutes (24 hours) to
hourly (7 days and daily history).

## Dashboards

Live dashboards rank game assets by figures from live servers, refreshed hourly.
Every dashboard is listed at GET /dashboards (`?format=json` for title, url,
description and cover). The Global Market (see above) is one of them and keeps its
address: /dashboards/market redirects to /market. The others live under
/dashboards/{slug}. Each one shows ranked lists side by side; every list has its
own query parameters (the second list's carry a prefix, such as `books_`):
`category`, `sort`, `order` (`desc` or `asc`) and `page` (10 rows a page, up to 50
rows). Assets only ever rank within their own category, and a ratio column ranks
only assets that meet the dashboard's minimum (the rest follow, flagged).

### Badlands PvP

Kills, deaths and kill/death ratio (KDR) in the Badlands (Desolation's Hand and
Lavalands) over the last 7 days, production servers only:

- HTML: GET /dashboards/badlands-pvp
- JSON: GET /dashboards/badlands-pvp?format=json
- Gear: `category` (`weapons`, `hats`, `armor`, `boots`, `offhand`), `sort`
  (`kills`, `deaths`, `kdr`), `order`, `page`
- Ability books (by the killer's and victim's class): `books_sort`,
  `books_order`, `books_page`

A kill counts for the gear the killer wore and the killer's class; a death for the
victim's. Item pages and ability book pages show the same figures in a header badge
with their rank in this list, and items repeat them under "Live Stats". Rows include
`name`, `url`, `kills`, `deaths`, `kdr` (null with no deaths), `kdrText`, and
`belowMinFights` (true for assets with fewer than `minFights` fights, which are not
ranked by KDR). Kills count base items, so variations and upgrades count toward
their base item, and a cosmetic hides the gear under it.

## Videos

Curated Vesteria videos from community content creators and the official
Vesteria channel (`official: true`):

- HTML: GET /videos and GET /videos/{slug}
- JSON: GET /videos?format=json and GET /videos/{slug}?format=json

Video records include `slug`, `youtubeId`, `title`, `author`, `publishedAt`,
`durationSeconds`, `official`, `tags`, `watchUrl`, `embedUrl`, `viewCount` (database page views),
`outboundClickCount` (click-throughs to YouTube), and `youtube` (YouTube view,
like, and comment counts, or null when unavailable).

### Becoming a featured Vesteria content creator

Any Vesteria player can submit their own YouTube videos to the official Vesteria
Database: log in at https://db.playvesteria.com/login, then submit at
https://db.playvesteria.com/videos/submit (see https://db.playvesteria.com/videos#submit-a-video).
Staff approve each video, and a creator can submit one video for approval at a
time. Approved videos appear on /videos with the creator's credit, under
Related Videos on the item, ability, monster, map and update pages the creator
chose. Staff can also share it in the #highlights channel of the Vesteria Discord
(https://discord.com/invite/vesteria).
Creators can use the site's game images and information in their videos under the
Vesteria Content License.

Effects may be item rewards, currency rewards, status effects, utility effects,
or joke effects. Item and currency effects link back to database item pages
when the target is known.

## Versions

Version pages describe known game update changes and link affected database
entries.

- Version index: GET /versions
- Version index JSON: GET /versions?format=json
- Version JSON: GET /versions/{version-number}?format=json

Version detail JSON includes `changes` (flat asset-specific records), `groups`
(the same changes organized for display), `notes`, and `footnotes`. Do not count
the grouped and flat copies twice. Change records link directly to their exact
asset or variation and include `changeType`, `summary`, and optional `details`.
New-asset entries can omit a full stat breakdown; fetch the linked asset page
for its current mechanics.

The page's single **Other Changes** section combines `notes` and `footnotes`.
These are release-wide prose, not additional per-asset change records. Shared
changes may intentionally appear here without a separate history entry on
every affected asset. `counts` describes the asset change records, not these
additional prose notes. Version 1323 and later numeric change details use
previous-to-new values where known; do not infer missing historical values
from the current page or assume older changelogs have the same detail coverage.

Use version data for changelog attribution, and current asset data for current
database facts. Avoid exposing internal/dev-facing terms when summarizing
changes for users.
